rows.description: Children given coloured bibs quickly cheer for their colour and decide their team is best, even though they were assigned at random. Belonging feels good and rapidly creates a sense of "us" and "them".
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Pride in the group and dislike of rivals [Actor]
rows.description: A child proudly supports their school house or cricket team and feels personally hurt when the rivals win. Group pride is warm but easily slips into mocking the other side.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager's mood rises and falls with the fortunes of their school, region or fandom, and they defend it fiercely against criticism. Group membership is a source of esteem, and insults to the group feel like insults to them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student feels like a Bihari in one setting, an engineer in another and a cricket fan in a third, and different identities come forward depending on who is present. Recognising this keeps any single label from taking over.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult notices the pull to favour their group, seeks a wider shared identity such as the same city, same team or fellow parents, and treats outsiders fairly. Pride in belonging need not require contempt for others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: contempt, pride, nostalgia

rows.subtype: Feeling poor next to a friend [Actor]
rows.description: A child who has enough at home feels sad on seeing a classmate's new bicycle and phone. The hurt comes from comparison, not from actual lack.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager compares their marks, clothes or family situation with peers who are a step ahead, and feels cheated even though their own situation is decent. Feeling deprived depends on who one looks at.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A graduate who expected a job like their seniors got, and did not, feels bitter and entitled to something being withheld. Frustration is sharper when a group seems to be getting what they believed they deserved.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A manager notices resentment in a team when one group gets raises or perks and another does not, even when everyone is paid fairly. Transparent criteria and honest explanation reduce the sense of being left behind.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult who catches themselves fuming at a peer's promotion asks what they actually have and what they can control, and compares to their own past. They keep ambition without letting envy set the mood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
